title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
spaceBreakdown:
- int parent[26]: fixed size → O(1)  
- no recursion, no extra containers → O(1)
approach: Equality equations bind variables into equivalence classes. By merging all “==” pairs with a Union‑Find structure we obtain these classes, then any “!=” pair that falls inside the same class makes the whole system impossible. This yields a linear‑time decision algorithm.
hints:
When we see “a==b” and also “b==c”, what must be true about “a” and “c”?  
The input size is at most 500 equations.

Use a Union‑Find (Disjoint Set Union) structure.  
Example: processing “a==b” merges a and b; later “b==c” merges the set {a,b} with c, so a, b, c are all in one component.

```
make each variable its own set
for each equation of form "x==y"
    union(x, y)
for each equation of form "x!=y"
    if find(x) == find(y) return false
return true
```

**Self‑inequality** - a variable cannot be unequal to itself  
`Input: ["a!=a"]` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: ignoring the case where the two letters are identical → returns true  

**Contradictory pair** - same pair appears both equal and not equal  
`Input: ["a==b","a!=b"]` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: checking “!=” equations before processing all “==” equations → returns true  

**Only inequalities** - no equalities at all  
`Input: ["a!=b","b!=c","c!=a"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: assuming a cycle of “!=” forces a contradiction → returns false  

**Duplicate equalities** - repeated “==” on the same variable  
`Input: ["a==a","a==a"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: treating “a==a” as a constraint that must be checked separately → may return false  

**Large component with external inequality** - many equalities forming one set, inequality to a different set  
`Input: ["a==b","b==c","d==e","a!=e"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: using a map<char,bool> that only records direct relations → returns false

followUps.q: What if the variable names are arbitrary strings and their total count can be up to 10⁵?
followUps.a: Map each distinct string to a numeric id (e.g., with unordered_map) and run Union‑Find on those ids. Time stays O(n α(V)) and space becomes O(V) for the map and DSU arrays.

followUps.q: How would you answer the question online, i.e., after each new equation you must report whether the system is still satisfiable?
followUps.a: Keep the DSU alive while processing the stream. After inserting a “==” equation, union the two sets; after a “!=” equation, immediately check whether the two variables already share a root. Each step costs O(α(V)) time and O(V) total space.

followUps.q: Suppose you also need to output one concrete integer assignment that satisfies all equations (when possible).
followUps.a: After building the DSU, assign a distinct integer (e.g., the component’s root index) to every component; all variables in the same component receive the same integer. This extra pass is O(V) time and O(V) space.
